2897.subject: Chemistry
2897.text: Identify the molecule in which the arrangement of electron pairs around the central atom is octahedral and shape is not octahedral.
2897.sol:
The arrangement of electron pairs around the central atom is octahedral and shape is not octahedral can be identified with the help of presence of lone pair (lp) of electrons and bond pair $(b p)$ of electrons associated with the central atom. The structure of given species are : (i) $\mathbf{S F}_6$ Central atom sulphur has 6 valence electrons, which are bonded with 6F-atoms, thus have octahedral shape.
(ii) $\mathbf{X e F}_{\mathbf{6}}$ Central atom, Xe have 8 valence electrons, out of which 6 are bonded with $6 \mathrm{ F}$-atoms and one $l p$ of electron is associated with Xe-atom. Thus, has distorted octahedral shape.
$\mathbf{B r F}_5$ Central atom $(\mathrm{Br})$ have 7 valence electrons, out of which 5 are bonded with $5 \mathrm{ F}$-atoms and one $l p$ of electron is associated with $\mathrm{Br}$-atom having square pyramidal shape.
$\mathbf{X e O}_{\mathbf{2}} \mathbf{F}_{\mathbf{4}}$ Central atom, Xe have 8 valence electrons, out of which 4 are bonded through 4-sigma $(\sigma)$ bonds with 4F-atoms and two oxygen atoms each having one sigma $(\sigma)$ bond and one pi $(\pi)$ bond is associated with Xe-atom. Thus, has octahedral shape.
Hence, option (c) is the correct answer.

8180.text: If \(c\) is a parameter, then the differential equation of the family of curves \(x²=c(y+c)^2\) is
8180.sol:
Given equation of the family of curves
$$\begin{aligned}& x²=c(y+c)^2 \\
& x=\sqrt{c}( y+c) \quad \ldots (i)
\end{aligned}$$\)
[on taking square root both sides]
Now, differentiate both sides w.r.t. \(x\), we get
$$\begin{aligned}\mathrm{I}& =\sqrt{c} \frac{d y}{d x}\\
\Rightarrow \quad \sqrt{c}& =\frac{d x}{d y} \quad \ldots ( ii)
\end{aligned}$$\)
From Eqs. (i) and (ii) on eliminating ' \(c\) ', we get
$$\begin{aligned}& x=\left(\frac{d x}{d y}\right)\left[ y+\left(\frac{d x}{d y}\right)^2\right] \\
& \Rightarrow \quad x\left(\frac{d y}{d x}\right)^3=y\left(\frac{d y}{d x}\right)^2+1 \\
& \Rightarrow \quad x\left(\frac{d y}{d x}\right)^3-y\left(\frac{d y}{d x}\right)^2-1=0 \\
\end{aligned}$$\)
Hence, option (4) is correct.

8567.subject: Mathematics
8567.text: If a point $P   \left(x, y\right)$ moves along the ellipse $\dfrac{x^{2}}{25} + \dfrac{y^{2}}{16} =1$ and if $C$ is the centre of the ellipse, then the sum of maximum and minimum values of $CP$ is
8567.sol:
Given equation of ellipse is $\dfrac{x^{2}}{25} + \dfrac{y^{2}}{16} = 1$.

Here $a = 5, b = 4$ and the centre of the ellipse is& $( 0, 0 )$.

The major axis of ellipse is along the $X -$axis and minor axis is along $Y -$axis.

The distance of point $P ( x, y )$ from the centre of the ellipse $C$ is maximum, only when the point& $P ( x, y )$ is on the endpoint of major axis (or at the vertex of ellipse along the major-axis).

Therefore, coordinate of point& $P$ at the endpoint of major-axis is& $( 5, 0 )$ or $( - 5, 0 )$.

Hence, maximum value of $CP$ is& $5$.

Similarly, the distance of point $P ( x, y )$ from the centre of the ellipse is minimum, only when the point& $P ( x, y )$ is on the endpoint of minor axis (or at the vertex of ellipse along the minor-axis).

Therefore, the coordinate of point& $P$ at the endpoint of minor-axis is& $( 4, 0 )$ or& $( - 4, 0 )$.

Hence, minimum value of $CP$ is& $4$.

Therefore, the sum of maximum and minimum values of CP $= a + b$

$= 5 + 4$

$= 9$.

10359.sol:
The word $MULTIPLE$ consists of three vowels that are placed at the ${2}^{nd}, {5}^{th}$ and& ${8}^{th}$ position.

The three& vowels can be arranged at their respective places in $3 !$ ways.

The remaining $5$ consonants can be arranged at their respective places in $\dfrac{5 !}{2 !} = 60$ ways

$∴$ Total number of arrangements $= 3 ! \times \dfrac{5 !}{2 !} = 360$

17559.text: Choose the correct stability order of the given free radicals.
17559.sol: In compounds (I), (III) and (IV) the -M effect and hyperconjugation effect are inoperative at meta positions. So we should consider the inductive effect of the groups. -I effect will decrease the stability of the free radical by withdrawing the electrons toward it itself. 19477.subject: Chemistry
19477.text:
Choose the correct reason:
o-hydroxybenzaldehyde is a liquid at room temperature while $p$-hydroxy-benzaldehyde is a high melting solid, because
options: p-hydroxybenzaldehyde, shows intramolecular hydrogen bonding while in o-hydroxy benzaldehyde there is stronger intermolecular hydrogen bonding
o-hydroxybenzaldehyde shows association of the molecules while in $p$-hydroxy benzaldehyde there is no association among the molecules
o-hydroxybenzaldehyde shows only weak Vanderwal's forces of attraction while in $p$-hydroxy benzaldehyde there is strong Vanderwal's forces of attraction in solid state
o-hydroxybenzaldehyde shows intramolecular hydrogen bonding while in $p$-hydroxy benzaldehyde there is no intramolecular hydrogen bonding
19477.sol:
o-hydroxybenzaldehyde exhibits intramolecular hydrogen bonding due to the proximity of the -OH and -CHO groups. This restricts the formation of intermolecular hydrogen bonds, resulting in weaker intermolecular forces and making it a liquid at room temperature.

In p-hydroxybenzaldehyde, the -OH and -CHO groups are far apart, so it cannot form intramolecular hydrogen bonds. Instead, it forms extensive intermolecular hydrogen bonds, leading to molecular association and a high melting point, making it a solid.

Thus, o-hydroxybenzaldehyde shows intramolecular hydrogen bonding while p-hydroxybenzaldehyde does not.

Answer: o-hydroxybenzaldehyde shows intramolecular hydrogen bonding while in $p$-hydroxy benzaldehyde there is no intramolecular hydrogen bonding

19550.subject: Chemistry
19550.text:
Identify the Carbonyl compound which will not be formed when hydration of Alkynes is carried out with dil. $\mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{SO}_4 / \mathrm{Hg}^{2+}$ at 333 K.
Acetone, Butanal, Ethanal, Butanone.
19550.sol:
Hydration of alkynes in the presence of dil. $\mathrm{H}_{2}\mathrm{SO}_{4}$ and $\mathrm{Hg}^{2+}$ follows Markovnikov addition of water to the triple bond, forming an enol intermediate which tautomerizes to a carbonyl compound.

For ethyne (HC \equiv CH$), hydration yields ethenol, which tautomerizes to ethanal (CH_{3}CHO$).

For propyne (CH_{3}C \equiv CH$), hydration yields prop-1-en-2-ol, which tautomerizes to acetone (CH_{3}COCH_{3}$).

For but-1-yne (CH_{3}CH_{2}C \equiv CH$), hydration yields but-1-en-2-ol, which tautomerizes to butanone (CH_{3}COCH_{2}CH_{3}$).

For but-2-yne (CH_{3}C \equiv CCH_{3}$), hydration yields but-2-en-2-ol, which tautomerizes to butanone (CH_{3}COCH_{2}CH_{3}$).

Butanal (CH_{3}CH_{2}CH_{2}CHO$) is an aldehyde with four carbon atoms. It would require the anti-Markovnikov addition of water to but-1-yne or the hydration of a terminal alkyne at the terminal carbon, which is not the product of the acid-catalyzed hydration of alkynes using \mathrm{Hg}^{2+}$ catalyst. Therefore, butanal is not formed.

Answer: Butanal

19568.text:
Identify the final product formed during the course of the given reactions.
Pentan-2-one $\xrightarrow{\mathrm{NaCN} / \mathrm{HCl}}[\mathrm{X}][\mathrm{X}] $\xrightarrow[95 \% $\mathrm{H}_3 \mathrm{PO}_4]{\Delta $$\text{$ with }$}[Y]$
19568.sol:
The reaction of pentan-2-one with NaCN/HCl is a cyanohydrin formation reaction. Pentan-2-one is $CH_3-C(=O)-CH_2-CH_2-CH_3$.

The nucleophilic addition of cyanide ion (CN^{-}$) to the carbonyl carbon of pentan-2-one followed by protonation yields 2-hydroxy-2-methylpentanenitrile, which is the intermediate [X]. The structure of [X] is $CH_3-C(OH)(CN)-CH_2-CH_2-CH_3$.

The subsequent reaction of [X] with 95% $H_3PO_4$ at elevated temperature is a dehydration reaction. The hydroxyl group (-OH) is protonated to form a good leaving group ($-OH_2^{+}$), which then leaves to form a carbocation at the C2 position. This is followed by the elimination of a proton from an adjacent carbon to form a double bond, resulting in an unsaturated nitrile.

The most stable alkene formed is the one where the double bond is conjugated with the nitrile group, or the more substituted alkene. Dehydration of 2-hydroxy-2-methylpentanenitrile leads to the formation of 2-methylpent-2-enenitrile, which is $CH_3-C(CN)=CH-CH_2-CH_3$.

Comparing this structure with the given options, the structure $CH_3-C(CN)=CH-CH_2-CH_3$ corresponds to the first option.

Answer: $

21905.subject: Mathematics
21905.text: A and B are two independent events. The probability of their simultaneous occurrence is $\dfrac{1}{8}$ and the probability that neither of them occurs is $\dfrac{3}{8}$. Then their individual probabilities are
21905.sol: Let $P(A) = x$ and $P(B) = y$. Since A$ and $B$ are independent events, $P(A \cap B) = P(A)P(B) = xy = $\dfrac{1}{8} .The probability that neither occurs is $P(A^{c} \cap B^{c}) = P(A^{c})P(B^{c}) = (1-x)(1-y) = $\dfrac{3}{8}$.Expanding the second equation: 1 - x - y + xy = $\dfrac{3}{8} .Substituting $xy = $\dfrac{1}{8}  into the equation: 1 - (x+y) + \dfrac{1}{8} = \dfrac{3}{8}$.Rearranging gives $x+y = 1 + \dfrac{1}{8} - \dfrac{3}{8} = 1 - \dfrac{2}{8} = 1 - \dfrac{1}{4} = \dfrac{3}{4}$.We have the sum $x+y = \dfrac{3}{4}$ and the product $xy = \dfrac{1}{8}$. These are the roots of the quadratic equation $t^2 - (x+y)t + xy = 0$, which is $t^2 - \dfrac{3}{4}t + \dfrac{1}{8} = 0$.Multiplying by 8: $8t^2 - 6t + 1 = 0$.Factoring the quadratic: $8t^2 - 4t - 2t + 1 = 0 \Rightarrow 4t(2t-1) - 1(2t-1) = 0 \Rightarrow (4t-1)(2t-1) = 0$.The roots are $t = \dfrac{1}{4}$ and $t = \dfrac{1}{2}$. Thus, the probabilities are $\dfrac{1}{2}$ and $\dfrac{1}{4}$.Answer: $\dfrac{1}{2} \text{ and } \dfrac{1}{4}$

22119.subject: Mathematics
22119.text: Let $\mathrm{ABC}$ be a triangle with equations of its sides $\mathrm{AB}, \mathrm{BC}$. $\mathrm{CA}$ respectively are $x-2=0, y-5=0$ and $5 x+2 y-10=0$. Then the orthocentre of triangle lies on the line
22119.sol:
The equations of the sides are $L_1: x - 2 = 0$, $L_2: y - 5 = 0$, and $L_3: 5x + 2y - 10 = 0$.

Find the vertices by solving the equations pairwise:
Vertex A is the intersection of $L_1$ and $L_3$: $x = 2$, $5(2) + 2y - 10 = 0 \Rightarrow 2y = 0 \Rightarrow y = 0$. So, $A = (2,0)$.
Vertex B is the intersection of $L_1$ and $L_2$: $x = 2$, $y = 5$. So, $B = (2,5)$.
Vertex C is the intersection of $L_2$ and $L_3$: $y = 5$, $5x + 2(5) - 10 = 0 \Rightarrow 5x = 0 \Rightarrow x = 0$. So, $C = (0,5)$.

The triangle ABC is a right-angled triangle at vertex B(2,5) because side AB is vertical (x=2$) and side BC is horizontal (y=5$).

In a right-angled triangle, the orthocentre is the vertex where the right angle is formed. Therefore, the orthocentre is $H = (2,5)$.

Check which line contains the point $(2,5)$:
For (1) $x - 2y = 2 - 2(5) = 2 - 10 = -8 eq 1$.
For (2) $x - y = 2 - 5 = -3 eq 0$.
For (3) $3x + y = 3(2) + 5 = 6 + 5 = 11 eq 1$.
For (4) $4x + y = 4(2) + 5 = 8 + 5 = 13$.

The point $(2,5)$ satisfies the equation $4x + y = 13$.

Answer: $4 x+y=13$

22518.chapter: Center of Mass, Momentum and Collision
22518.text: The separation between C and O atoms in CO is 0.12 nm. The distance of C atom from the centre of mass is
22518.sol:
Let $m_{C}$ be the mass of the carbon atom and $m_{O}$ be the mass of the oxygen atom. The atomic mass of carbon is $12 \text{ u}$ and the atomic mass of oxygen is $16 \text{ u}$.

Let the position of the carbon atom be $x_{C} = 0$ and the position of the oxygen atom be $x_{O} = d = 0.12 \text{ nm}$.

The centre of mass $X_{CM}$ is given by the formula $X_{CM} = \dfrac{m_{C}x_{C} + m_{O}x_{O}}{m_{C} + m_{O}}$.

Substituting the values, $X_{CM} = \dfrac{12 \times 0 + 16 \times 0.12}{12 + 16} = \dfrac{16 \times 0.12}{28}$.

$X_{CM} = \dfrac{4 \times 0.12}{7} = \dfrac{0.48}{7} \approx 0.06857 \text{ nm}$.

Rounding to 2 decimal places, the distance of the carbon atom from the centre of mass is approximately $0.07 \text{ nm}$.

Answer: 0.07 nm

23427.text: A singer, during his performance, stands on the edge of a circular turntable, and begins to walk along its edge with a speed of $1.5\ ms^{-1}$ relative to the ground. The turn table is mounted on a frictionless vertical axle. Its radius R = 3m and its moment of inertia about the axle is 150 kg m². It is initially at rest. If the mass of the singer is 75kg, the time taken by the man to complete one revolution is:
23427.sol:
Given:
Speed of the singer relative to the ground, $v = 1.5\text{ m s}^{-1}$
Radius of the circular turntable, $R = 3\text{ m}$

The problem asks for the time taken by the singer to complete one revolution. Since the speed of the singer is given relative to the ground, the time taken to complete one revolution relative to the ground can be calculated directly using the circumference of the circular path.

The total distance covered in one revolution is $2\pi R$.

Time taken $T = \dfrac{2\pi R}{v}$

Substituting the given values:
$T = \dfrac{2\pi \times 3}{1.5}$

$T = 4\pi$

$T = 4 \times 3.1416 \approx 12.57\text{ s}$

The mass of the singer and the moment of inertia of the turntable are extraneous information provided as distractors, as the ground speed is already explicitly given.

Answer: $12.57$s

28140.subject: Chemistry
28140.text:
Consider the reaction $aX \rightarrow bY$, for which the rate constant at $30°C$ is $1 \times 10^{-3}$ mol$^{-1}$ L s$^{-1}$. Which of the following statements are true?
A. When concentration of 'X' is increased to four times, the rate of reaction becomes $16$ times.
B. The reaction is a second order reaction.
C. The half-life period is independent of the concentration of X.
D. Decomposition of $N_2 O_5$ is an example of the above reaction.
E. $\ln\dfrac{[R_o]}{[R]}$ vs time is valid for the above reaction.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: A, B, D and E Only
28140.sol:
The unit of the rate constant $k$ is mol$^{-1}$ L s$^{-1}$.

The general unit of the rate constant for an $n$-th order reaction is (mol L$^{-1}$)$^{1-n}$ s$^{-1}$.

Equating the powers of the concentration units, we get $1-n = -1 \Rightarrow n = 2$.

Thus, the reaction is a second-order reaction. Statement B is correct.

For a second-order reaction, Rate $= k[X]^2$. When the concentration of $X$ is increased to $4$ times, the new rate is $k(4[X])^2 = 16k[X]^2$, which is $16$ times the original rate. Statement A is correct.

The half-life of a second-order reaction is $t_{1/2} = \dfrac{1}{k[X]_0}$, which depends inversely on the initial concentration. Statement C is incorrect.

The decomposition of $N_2O_5$ is a well-known first-order reaction. Statement D is incorrect.

The equation $\ln\dfrac{[R_o]}{[R]} = kt$ represents the integrated rate law for a first-order reaction, not a second-order reaction. Statement E is incorrect.

Therefore, only statements A and B are correct.

Answer: A and B Only

30394.text: $R_f$ value for $2$-methylpropene in a solvent system (Ethyl acetate + ether) is $0.42$. $2$-methylpropene is treated with dilute $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$ to give major organic product (X). $R_f$ value for (X) in the same solvent system under identical condition will be:
30394.sol:
$2$-methylpropene reacts with dilute $H_2SO_4$ to undergo hydration, forming tert-butyl alcohol as the major product (X).

The reaction is:

$CH_2=C(CH_3)_2 \xrightarrow{\text{dil. } H_2SO_4} (CH_3)_3C-OH$

Product (X) is an alcohol, which is significantly more polar than the starting alkene due to the presence of the $-OH$ group. In normal phase chromatography, the stationary phase (such as silica gel) is highly polar. The polar $-OH$ group forms strong hydrogen bonds with the stationary phase, causing the alcohol to be adsorbed more strongly than the non-polar alkene.

Consequently, the alcohol travels a shorter distance along the chromatography plate, resulting in a lower $R_f$ value compared to the alkene.

Since the $R_f$ value of $2$-methylpropene is $0.42$, the $R_f$ value of product (X) must be less than $0.42$. Among the given choices, only $0.12$ satisfies this condition.

Answer: $0.12$

36330.subject: Mathematics
36330.text: The number of ways of forming a queue of $4$ boys and $3$ girls such that all the girls are not together, is:
36330.sol:
Total number of boys $= 4$

Total number of girls $= 3$

Total number of children $= 7$

Total number of ways to arrange $7$ children in a queue $= 7! = 5040$

To find the number of ways where all $3$ girls are together, consider the $3$ girls as a single unit.

Total number of units to arrange $= 4$ boys $+ 1$ unit of girls $= 5$ units.

Number of ways to arrange these $5$ units $= 5! = 120$

Number of ways to arrange the $3$ girls among themselves $= 3! = 6$

Total number of ways where all girls are together $= 5! \times 3! = 120 \times 6 = 720$

Number of ways such that all the girls are not together $= \text{Total ways} - \text{Ways where all girls are together}$

$= 5040 - 720 = 4320$

Answer: $4320$

36615.subject: Mathematics
36615.text: In a binomial distribution $B ( n, p )$, the sum and product of the mean & variance are $5$ and $6$ respectively, then find $6 ( n + p - q )$ is equal to :-
36615.sol:
For the binomial distribution $B ( n, p )$,

Mean $= np$ and Variance $= npq$

Sum of mean and variance $= np + npq = 5$

$⇒ np ( 1 + q ) = 5$

$⇒ {n}^{2}{p}^{2} ( 1 + q{)}^{2} = 25$ ....(1)

Product of mean and variance $= np . npq = 6$

$⇒ {n}^{2}{p}^{2}q = 6$ ....(2)

Put the value of ${n}^{2}{p}^{2}$ from equation (2) into equation (1):

$\dfrac{6}{q} ( 1 + q{)}^{2} = 25$

$⇒ 6{q}^{2} + 12q + 6 = 25q$

$⇒ 6{q}^{2} - 13q + 6 = 0$

$⇒ ( 3q - 2 ) ( 2q - 3 ) = 0$

$⇒ q = \dfrac{2}{3}, \dfrac{3}{2}$ where $q = \dfrac{2}{3}$ accepted

$∴ p = \dfrac{1}{3} ⇒ n \cdot \dfrac{1}{3} + n \cdot \dfrac{1}{3} \cdot \dfrac{2}{3} = 5$

$⇒ \dfrac{3n + 2n}{9} = 5$

$⇒ n = 9$

Therefore,

$6 ( n + p - q ) = 6\left(9 + \dfrac{1}{3} - \dfrac{2}{3}\right) = 52$

36688.text: Let ${B}_{i}\left(i = 1, 2, 3\right)$ be three independent events in a sample space. The probability that only ${B}_{1}$ occur is $\alpha,$ only ${B}_{2}$ occurs is $\beta$ and only ${B}_{3}$ occurs is $\gamma .$ Let $p$ be the probability that none of the events ${B}_{i}$ occurs and these $4$ probabilities satisfy the equations $\left(\alpha - 2\beta\right)p = \alpha\beta$ and $\left(\beta - 3\gamma\right)p = 2\beta\gamma$ (All the probabilities are assumed to lie in the interval $\left\left(0, 1\right)\right)$ Then $\dfrac{P\left({B}_{1}\right)}{P\left({B}_{3}\right)}$ is equal to______.
36688.sol:
Let $P\left({B}_{1}\right) = {p}_{1}, P\left({B}_{2}\right) = {p}_{2}, P\left({B}_{3}\right) = {p}_{3}$

given that ${p}_{1}\left(1 - {p}_{2}\right)\left(1 - {p}_{3}\right) = \alpha \ldots \left(i\right)$

${p}_{2}\left(1 - {p}_{1}\right)\left(1 - {p}_{3}\right) = \beta \ldots \left(ii\right)$

${p}_{3}\left(1 - {p}_{1}\right)\left(1 - {p}_{2}\right) = \gamma \ldots \left(iii\right)$

and $\left(1 - {p}_{1}\right)\left(1 - {p}_{2}\right)\left(1 - {p}_{3}\right) = p \ldots \left(iv\right)$

$⇒ \dfrac{{p}_{1}}{1 - {p}_{1}} = \dfrac{\alpha}{p}, \dfrac{{p}_{2}}{1 - {p}_{2}} = \dfrac{\beta}{p}$ and $\dfrac{{p}_{3}}{1 - {p}_{3}} = \dfrac{\gamma}{p}$

Also $\beta = \dfrac{\alphap}{\alpha + 2p} = \dfrac{3\gammap}{p - 2\gamma}$

$⇒ \alphap - 2\alpha\gamma = 3\alpha\gamma + 6p\gamma$

$⇒ \alphap - 6p\gamma = 5\alpha\gamma$

$⇒ \dfrac{{p}_{1}}{1 - {p}_{1}} - \dfrac{6{p}_{3}}{1 - {p}_{3}} = \dfrac{5{p}_{1}{p}_{3}}{\left(1 - {p}_{1}\right)\left(1 - {p}_{3}\right)}$

$⇒ {p}_{1} - 6{p}_{3} = 0$

$⇒ \dfrac{{p}_{1}}{{p}_{3}} = 6$

40683.subject: Physics
40683.text:
A uniformly charged solid sphere of radius R has potential ${V}_{0}$ (measured with respect to $\infty$ ) on its surface. For this sphere the equipotential surfaces with potential $\dfrac{3{V}_{0}}{2}, \dfrac{5{V}_{0}}{4}, \dfrac{3{V}_{0}}{4}$ and $\dfrac{{V}_{0}}{4}$ have radius ${R}_{1}$ , ${R}_{2}, {R}_{3}$ and ${R}_{4}$ respectively. Then

Note : This question had two option correct at the time of examination. Proper corrections are made in the question to avoid it.
40683.sol:
Potential for uniformly charged solid sphere

$\text{v} = \dfrac{1}{4 \pi {ε}_{0}} \dfrac{\text{Q}}{\text{r}}$ outside i.e r > R

$\text{v} = \dfrac{1}{4 \pi {ε}_{0}} \dfrac{\text{Q}}{\text{R}}$ on the surface

$\text{v} = \dfrac{1}{4 \pi {ε}_{0}} \dfrac{\text{Q}}{\text{R}} \left[\dfrac{3}{2} - \dfrac{1}{2} \dfrac{{\text{r}}^{2}}{{\text{R}}^{2}}\right]$ inside i.e. r < R

Clearly

$\dfrac{3 {\text{v}}_{0}}{2} \text{,} \dfrac{5 {\text{v}}_{0}}{4}$ are inside potentials $\left[∵ > {\text{v}}_{0}\right]$

$\dfrac{3 {\text{v}}_{0}}{4} \text{,} \dfrac{{\text{v}}_{0}}{4}$ are outside potentials $\left[∵ < {\text{v}}_{0}\right]$

To get ${\text{R}}_{1}$: $\dfrac{3 {\text{v}}_{0}}{2} = \dfrac{1}{4 \pi {ε}_{0}} \dfrac{\text{Q}}{\text{R}} \left[\dfrac{3}{2} - \dfrac{1}{2} \dfrac{{\text{R}}_{1}^{2}}{{\text{R}}^{2}}\right]$

${\text{where, v}}_{0} = \dfrac{1}{4 \pi {ε}_{0}} \dfrac{\text{Q}}{\text{R}}$

$\dfrac{3}{2 \times 4 \pi {ε}_{0}} \dfrac{\text{Q}}{\text{R}} = \dfrac{1}{4 \pi {ε}_{0}} \dfrac{\text{Q}}{\text{R}} \left[\dfrac{3}{2} - \dfrac{1}{2} \dfrac{{\text{R}}_{1}^{2}}{{\text{R}}^{2}}\right]$

$\dfrac{3}{2} = \dfrac{3}{2} - \dfrac{1}{2} \dfrac{{\text{R}}_{1}^{2}}{{\text{R}}^{2}} ⇒ {\text{R}}_{1} = 0$

To get ${\text{R}}_{2}$: $\dfrac{5}{4} {\text{v}}_{0} = \dfrac{1}{4 \pi {ε}_{0}} \dfrac{\text{Q}}{\text{R}} \left[\dfrac{3}{2} - \dfrac{1}{2} \dfrac{{\text{R}}_{2}^{2}}{{\text{R}}^{2}}\right]$

$\dfrac{5}{4} \dfrac{1}{4 \pi {ε}_{0}} \dfrac{\text{Q}}{\text{R}} = \dfrac{1}{4 \pi {ε}_{0}} \dfrac{\text{Q}}{\text{R}} \left[\dfrac{3}{2} - \dfrac{1}{2} \dfrac{{\text{R}}_{2}^{2}}{{\text{R}}^{2}}\right]$

$\dfrac{5}{4} = \dfrac{3}{2} - \dfrac{1}{2} \dfrac{{\text{R}}_{2}^{2}}{{\text{R}}^{2}}$

$\dfrac{1}{2} \dfrac{{\text{R}}_{2}^{2}}{{\text{R}}^{2}} = \dfrac{1}{4 }$$⇒$ ${\text{R}}_{2} = \dfrac{\text{R}}{\sqrt{2}}$

To get ${\text{R}}_{3}$ : $\dfrac{3 {\text{v}}_{0}}{4} = \dfrac{1}{4 \pi {ε}_{0}} \dfrac{\text{Q}}{{\text{R}}_{3}}$

$\dfrac{3}{4} \dfrac{1}{4 \pi {ε}_{0}} \dfrac{\text{Q}}{\text{R}} = \dfrac{1}{4 \pi {ε}_{0}} \dfrac{\text{Q}}{{\text{R}}_{3}}$

$\dfrac{3}{4 \text{R}} = \dfrac{1}{{\text{R}}_{3}}$

${\text{R}}_{3} = \dfrac{4}{3} \text{R}$

To get ${\text{R}}_{4}$: $\dfrac{{\text{v}}_{0}}{4} = \dfrac{1}{4 \pi {ε}_{0}} \dfrac{\text{Q}}{{\text{R}}_{4}}$

$\dfrac{1}{4} \times \dfrac{1}{4 \pi {ε}_{0}} \dfrac{\text{Q}}{\text{R}} = \dfrac{1}{4 \pi {ε}_{0}} \dfrac{\text{Q}}{{\text{R}}_{4}}$

${\text{R}}_{4} = 4 \text{R}$

${\text{R}}_{4} - {\text{R}}_{3} = 4 \text{R} - \dfrac{4 \text{R}}{3} = \dfrac{8 \text{R}}{3} > {\text{R}}_{2}$

${\text{R}}_{1} = 0$ and ${\text{R}}_{2} < \left({\text{R}}_{4} - {\text{R}}_{3}\right)$

42930.text: The refractive index of prism is $\mu=\sqrt{3}$ and the ratio of the angle of minimum deviation to the angle of prism is one. The value of angle of prism is _______.
42930.sol:
For $\delta_{\min } \begin{aligned} & \mathrm{i}=\mathrm{e} \\ & \mathrm{r}_1=\mathrm{r}_2=\frac{\mathrm{A}}{2} \\ & \frac{\delta_{\min }}{\mathrm{A}}=1 \\ & \frac{2 \mathrm{i}-\mathrm{A}}{\mathrm{A}}=1 \\ & \\ & 2 \mathrm{i}=2 \mathrm{~A} \\ & \mathrm{i}=\mathrm{A} \end{aligned}$
Snell's law $\begin{aligned} & 1 \times \sin i=\mu \sin r \\ & \sin i=\mu \sin \left(\frac{A}{2}\right) \\ & \sin A=\mu \sin \left(\frac{A}{2}\right) \\ & 2 \sin \frac{A}{2} \cos \frac{A}{2}=\sqrt{3} \sin \left(\frac{A}{2}\right) \\ & \cos \left(\frac{A}{2}\right)=\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2} \\ & \therefore \frac{A}{2}=30^{\circ} \\ & \therefore A=60^{\circ} \end{aligned}$

According to the law of conservation of momentum, we get

or $\left(\frac{m_1}{m_2}\right)=\left(\frac{v_2}{v_1}\right)$
But $m=\frac{4}{3} \pi r^3 \rho \text{ or } m \propto r^3$
$\begin{array}{ll}\Rightarrow & \frac{m_1}{m_2}=\frac{r_1^3}{r_2^3} \\ \therefore & \frac{r_1^3}{r_2^3}=\frac{V_2}{V_1}=\frac{1}{2} \\ \Rightarrow & \frac{r_1}{r_2}=\left(\frac{1}{2}\right)^{1 / 3} \\ \therefore & r_1: r_2=1:(2)^{1 / 3}\end{array}$

46549.subject: Physics
46549.text: A telescope has focal length of objective and eye-piece as 200 cm and 5 cm respectively. What is magnification of telescope?
46549.sol:
In relaxed eye state of telescope or when final image is formed at infinity, the magnification of telescope is given by
$|M|=\frac{f_o}{f_e}$
where $\begin{aligned} f_o & =\text{ focal length$ of $objective }=200 \mathrm{ cm} \\ f_e & =\text{ focal length of eye-piece }=5 \mathrm{ cm}\end{aligned}$
Hence, $|M|=\frac{200}{5}=40 |M|=\frac{200}{5}=40$
Note : The aperture of the objective lens is kept large so that more and more rays coming from the heavenly body may enter the telescope and a bright image is formed by the objective lens. The aperture of the eye lens is kept comparatively small so that all the rays may enter the eye.

52099.text: Four electrons, each of mass ${m}_{e}$ are in a one dimensional box of size $L$. Assume that, the electrons are non-interacting, obey the Pauli exclusion principle and are described by standing de Broglie waves confined within the box. For an electron described by standing waves confined within a box of length $L$, the wave can occupy only states for which

$L = \dfrac{n\lambda}{2}$, where $n = 1, 2, 3 \ldots$

$\lambda = \dfrac{h}{p} = \dfrac{h}{2mE}$

From above two equations, we have

${E}_{n} = \left(\dfrac{h2}{9mL^{2}}\right)n^{2}$

(where, $n = 1, 2, 3 \ldots$)

Now, ground state energy is obtained by substituting $n = 1$.

$∴ {U}_{0} = {E}_{1} = \dfrac{h2}{8mL^{2}}$

Energy of first excited state,

${E}_{2} = \dfrac{h2}{8mL^{2}} \times {2}^{2}$

$= 4{U}_{0} = {U}_{0} + 3\alpha$

Also, energy for second excited state,

${E}_{3} = \dfrac{h2}{8mL^{2}} \times {3}^{2}$

$= 9{U}_{0} = {U}_{0} + 8\alpha$

54936.subject: Chemistry
54936.text: Which from following is called as Lucas reagent?
54936.sol:
Lucas reagent is a mixture of concentrated hydrochloric acid $(\mathrm{HCl})$ and zinc chloride $\left(\mathrm{ZnCl}_2\right)$. It is used for the differentiation of alcohols based on their reactivity. The test is particularly used to distinguish between primary, secondary, and tertiary alcohols.
- Tertiary alcohols react almost immediately with Lucas reagent to form alkyl chlorides (substitution of the hydroxyl group with a chlorine atom).
- Secondary alcohols react after some time, typically within 5-10 minutes.
- Primary alcohols react very slowly, if at all, and may require heating.

59931.subject: Chemistry
59931.text: Calculate the change in internal energy of the system if 20 kJ work is done on the system and it releases 10 kJ heat in a particular reaction.
59931.sol:
The first law of thermodynamics states that the change in internal energy $\Delta U$ of a system equals the heat added to it plus the work done on it: $\Delta U = q + w$.

Work done on the system is positive, so $w = +20 \text{kJ}$. Heat released by the system is negative, so $q = -10 \text{kJ}$.

Substituting into the equation:

$\Delta U = -10 + 20 = 10 \text{kJ}$

The change in internal energy is 10 kJ.

60183.subject: Mathematics
60183.text: The line $x + y = 0$ touches the curve $y^2 = ax^3 + b$ at $(1,-1)$ then values of $a$ and $b$ respectively are...........
60183.sol:
Since the point $(1, -1)$ lies on the curve $y^2 = ax^3 + b$, substituting $x = 1 and y = -1$ gives:

$(-1)^2 = a(1)^3 + b$

$a + b = 1$

Differentiating the equation of the curve with respect to $x$ gives:

$2y \dfrac{dy}{dx} = 3ax^2$

$\dfrac{dy}{dx} = \dfrac{3ax^2}{2y}$

The slope of the tangent at $(1, -1)$ is:

$\left. \dfrac{dy}{dx} \right|_{(1, -1)} = \dfrac{3a(1)^2}{2(-1)} = -\dfrac{3a}{2}$

The given tangent line is $x + y = 0$, which has a slope of $-1$. Equating the slopes gives:

$-\dfrac{3a}{2} = -1$

$a = \dfrac{2}{3}$

Substituting the value of $a$ into $a + b = 1$ gives:

$\dfrac{2}{3} + b = 1$

$b = \dfrac{1}{3}$

Answer: $\dfrac{2}{3}, \dfrac{1}{3}$

60184.subject: Mathematics
60184.text: An aeroplane at an altitude of 1 km is flying horizontally at 600 km / hr, passes directly over an observer. Then the rate at which it is approaching the observer when it is 1250 meters away from him is........
60184.sol:
Let the horizontal distance of the aeroplane from the observer be $x$ km and the actual distance be $s$ km.

The altitude of the aeroplane is $h = 1$ km.

From the right-angled triangle formed by the observer, the aeroplane, and the point on the ground directly below the aeroplane, we have:

$s^2 = x^2 + 1^2$

Differentiating with respect to time $t$, we get:

$2s \dfrac{ds}{dt} = 2x \dfrac{dx}{dt}$

$\dfrac{ds}{dt} = \dfrac{x}{s} \dfrac{dx}{dt}$

We are given the horizontal velocity $\dfrac{dx}{dt} = 600$ km/hr.

When the distance $s = 1250$ m $= 1.25$ km, the horizontal distance $x$ is:

$x = \sqrt{s^2 - 1^2} = \sqrt{1.25^2 - 1} = \sqrt{1.5625 - 1} = \sqrt{0.5625} = 0.75$ km

Substituting the values into the derivative equation:

$\dfrac{ds}{dt} = \dfrac{0.75}{1.25} \times 600$

$\dfrac{ds}{dt} = \dfrac{3}{5} \times 600 = 360$ km/hr

Answer: $360\ km/hr$

60195.subject: Mathematics
60195.text: Let $g(x) = f(x) + f(1-x)$ and $f''(x) < 0, 0 \leq x \leq 1$, then $\ldots$
60195.sol:
Given $g(x) = f(x) + f(1-x)$

Differentiating with respect to $x$, we get:

$g'(x) = f'(x) - f'(1-x)$

It is given that $f''(x) \lt 0$ for $0 \leq x \leq 1$, which implies that $f'(x)$ is a strictly decreasing function on $[0, 1]$.

For $g(x)$ to be increasing, $g'(x) \gt 0$:

$f'(x) - f'(1-x) \gt 0$

$f'(x) \gt f'(1-x)$

Since $f'(x)$ is strictly decreasing, the input values must satisfy the reverse inequality:

$x \lt 1 - x$

$2x \lt 1 \Rightarrow x \lt \dfrac{1}{2}$

Thus, $g(x)$ is increasing on $\left[0, \dfrac{1}{2}\right]$.

For $g(x)$ to be decreasing, $g'(x) \lt 0$:

$f'(x) - f'(1-x) \lt 0$

$f'(x) \lt f'(1-x)$

Again, since $f'(x)$ is strictly decreasing, the input values must satisfy:

$x \gt 1 - x$

$2x \gt 1 \Rightarrow x \gt \dfrac{1}{2}$

Thus, $g(x)$ is decreasing on $\left[\dfrac{1}{2}, 1\right]$.

Answer: $g(x)$ decreases on $\left[\dfrac{1}{2}, 1\right]$ and g(x) increases on $\left[0, \dfrac{1}{2}\right]$

61236.text: If $\left[\begin{array}{lll}1 & 3 & 3 \\ 1 & 4 & 4 \\ 1 & 3 & 4\end{array}$\right]$\left[\begin{array}{l}x \\ y \\ z\end{array}$\right]=$\left[\begin{array}{l}12 \\ 15 \\ 13\end{array}$\right]$, then the value of $x^2+y^2+z^2=
61236.sol:
The matrix equation corresponds to the system:

$x + 3y + 3z = 12$

$x + 4y + 4z = 15$

$x + 3y + 4z = 13$

Subtracting the first equation from the second gives: $y + z = 3$.

Subtracting the first from the third yields: $z = 1$.

Substituting $z = 1$ into $y + z = 3$ gives $y = 2$.

Then, from the first equation: $x + 3(2) + 3(1) = 12$, so $x = 3$.

Thus, $x^{2} + y^{2} + z^{2} = 3^{2} + 2^{2} + 1^{2} = 9 + 4 + 1 = 14$.

Final answer: $\boxed{D}$

61498.text: The general solution of $\sin ^{-1}\left(\frac{d y}{d x}\right)=x+y$ is
61498.sol: $\begin{aligned} & \sin ^{-1}\left(\frac{d y}{d x}\right)=x+y \\ & \therefore \frac{d y}{d x}=\sin (x+y) \\ & \text{ Put } x+y=t \quad \Rightarrow 1+\frac{d y}{d x}=\frac{d t}{d x} \\ & \therefore \frac{d t}{d x}-1=\sin t \Rightarrow \frac{d t}{d x}=1+\sin t \\ & \therefore \int \frac{d t}{1+\sin t}=\int d x \\ & \therefore \int \frac{(1-\sin t) d t}{1-\sin } t=\int d x \Rightarrow \int \frac{1-\sin t}{\cos ^2 t} d t=\int d x \\ & \Rightarrow \int\left(\sec ^2 t-\operatorname{sect} \tan t\right) d t=\int d x \\ & \therefore \tan t-\sec t=x+c \\ & \therefore \tan (x+y)-\sec (x+y)=x+c\end{aligned}$

62532.sol:
The principal value branch of $\cos^{-1}x$ is $[0, \pi]$.

$\cos^{-1}\left(\cos\dfrac{4\pi}{3}\right) = \cos^{-1}\left(\cos\left(2\pi - \dfrac{2\pi}{3}\right)\right) = \cos^{-1}\left(\cos\dfrac{2\pi}{3}\right) = \dfrac{2\pi}{3}$

The principal value branch of $\sin^{-1}x$ is $\left[-\dfrac{\pi}{2}, \dfrac{\pi}{2}\right]$.

$\sin^{-1}\left(\sin\dfrac{4\pi}{3}\right) = \sin^{-1}\left(\sin\left(\pi + \dfrac{\pi}{3}\right)\right) = \sin^{-1}\left(-\sin\dfrac{\pi}{3}\right) = \sin^{-1}\left(\sin\left(-\dfrac{\pi}{3}\right)\right) = -\dfrac{\pi}{3}$

Adding the two values:

$\dfrac{2\pi}{3} - \dfrac{\pi}{3} = \dfrac{\pi}{3}$

Answer: $\dfrac{\pi}{3}$

62960.subject: Mathematics
62960.text:
Consider the following three statements
(A) If $3+2=7$ then $4+3=8$.
(B) If $5+2=7$ then earth is flat.
(C) If both (A) and (B) are true then $5+6=11$.
Which of the following statements is correct?
options: (A) and (C) are true while (B) is false.
(A) is true while (B) and (C) are false.
(A) is false but (B) and (C) are true.
62960.sol:
A conditional statement $P \implies Q$ is false only when $P$ is true and $Q$ is false. In all other cases, it is true.

Statement A: If $3+2=7$ then $4+3=8$.
The antecedent $3+2=7$ is false, and the consequent $4+3=8$ is also false. Since the antecedent is false, the entire implication is true.

Statement B: If $5+2=7$ then Earth is flat.
The antecedent $5+2=7$ is true, but the consequent "Earth is flat" is false. With a true antecedent and false consequent, the implication is false.

Statement C: If both A and B are true then $5+6=11$.
The antecedent "both A and B are true" is false because B is false, and the consequent $5+6=11$ is true. Since the antecedent is false, the implication is true.

Therefore, A and C are true while B is false, which corresponds to option A.

63621.subject: Mathematics
63621.text: A player tosses two coins. He wins Rs. 10, if 2 heads appears, Rs. 5, if one head appear and Rs. 2 if no head appears. Then variance of winning amount is
63621.sol:
Expected value and variance for the two-coin toss game

In a game where two fair coins are tossed, the possible outcomes are $HH$, $HT$, $TH$, and $TT$, each with probability $\frac{1}{4}$.
The winning amount $X$ is $10$ for $HH$ ($P(X=10)=1/4$), $5$ for $HT$ or $TH$ ($P(X=5)=1/2$), and $2$ for $TT$ ($P(X=2)=1/4$).

The expected value is $E(X) = \sum x \cdot P(X=x) = 10 \cdot \frac{1}{4} + 5 \cdot \frac{1}{2} + 2 \cdot \frac{1}{4} = 5.5$.

$E(X^2) = 100 \cdot \frac{1}{4} + 25 \cdot \frac{1}{2} + 4 \cdot \frac{1}{4} = 38.5$.

Variance is $\text{Var}(X) = E(X^2) - [E(X)]^2 = 38.5 - (5.5)^2 = 8.25$.

Hence, the variance is $\boxed{\text{C}}$.

64437.text: The length of the foot of the perpendicular from the point $\left(1, \frac{3}{2}, 2\right)$ to the plane $2 x-2 y+4 z+17=0$ is
64437.sol:
The perpendicular distance from point $P(x_1, y_1, z_1)$ to the plane $Ax + By + Cz + D = 0$ is given by $d = \frac{|Ax_1 + By_1 + Cz_1 + D|}{\sqrt{A^2 + B^2 + C^2}}$.

For point $P \left(1, \frac{3}{2},$2\right)$ and plane $2x - 2y + 4z + 17 = 0$, we substitute $A = 2$, $B = -2$, $C = 4$, $D = 17$.

Evaluating the numerator:
$|2(1) - 2\$left(\frac{3}{2}\right) +$4(2) + 17| = |2 - 3 + 8 + 17| = |24| = 24$.

The denominator simplifies to:
\sqrt{2^2 + (-2)^2 + 4^2} = \sqrt{4 + 4 + 16} = \sqrt{24} =$==2\sqrt{6}.$

Thus, the distance is
$d = $\frac{24}{2\sqrt{6}} = \frac{12}{\sqrt{6}} = \frac{12\sqrt{6}}{6} =$==2\sqrt{6}.$

This result corresponds to option D.

68602.subject: Physics
68602.text: The half-life of the isotope ${}_{11}\text{Na}^{24}$ is 15 hr. How much time does it take for $\left(\dfrac{7}{8}\right)^{\text{th}}$ of a sample of this isotope to decay ?
68602.sol:
Fraction of the sample decayed is $\dfrac{7}{8}$.

Fraction of the sample remaining is $1 - \dfrac{7}{8} = \dfrac{1}{8}$.

The amount of substance remaining after time $t$ is given by $N = N_0 \left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right)^{\dfrac{t}{T_{1/2}}}$.

Substituting the values, we get $\dfrac{1}{8} = \left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right)^{\dfrac{t}{15}}$.

$\left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right)^3 = \left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right)^{\dfrac{t}{15}}$

$\dfrac{t}{15} = 3$

$t = 45$ hr.

Answer: $45$ hour

69161.subject: Physics
69161.text: Four point masses m, 2m, 3m and 4m are kept at the corners A, B, C and D respectively of a square ABCD of side '$b$'. The moment of inertia of the system about an axis perpendicular to the plane of the square and passing through the point D is
69161.sol:
The moment of inertia of a system of point masses is given by $I = \sum m_i r_i^2$, where $r_i$ is the perpendicular distance of the $i$-th mass from the axis of rotation.

The axis of rotation is perpendicular to the plane of the square and passes through point D. The distances of the masses from the axis are:

For mass at A (m_A = m$): $r_A = b$

For mass at B (m_B = 2m$): $r_B = b\sqrt{2}$ (diagonal of the square)

For mass at C (m_C = 3m$): $r_C = b$

For mass at D (m_D = 4m$): $r_D = 0$

Substituting these values into the formula:

$I = m(b)^2 + 2m(b\sqrt{2})^2 + 3m(b)^2 + 4m(0)^2$

$I = mb^2 + 2m(2b^2) + 3mb^2 + 0$

$I = mb^2 + 4mb^2 + 3mb^2 = 8mb^2$

Answer: $8\ mb^2$

69466.text: Which of the following statements is $\underline{TRUE}$ for n-type semiconductor?
options: Holes are majority carriers and trivalent atoms are dopants.
Electrons are majority carriers and trivalent atoms are dopants.
Holes are minority carriers and pentavalent atoms are dopants.
Electrons are minority carriers and pentavalent atoms are dopants.
69466.sol:
An n-type semiconductor is formed by doping a pure semiconductor with pentavalent impurities, which serve as donor atoms contributing free electrons. This results in electrons becoming the majority charge carriers, while holes remain as minority carriers due to their lower concentration from thermal generation.

Assessing the options:

A incorrectly identifies holes as majority carriers and trivalent atoms as dopants, which corresponds to p-type semiconductors.

B correctly identifies electrons as majority carriers but incorrectly specifies trivalent dopants.

C correctly states that holes are minority carriers and pentavalent atoms are the dopants.

D incorrectly identifies electrons as minority carriers, despite their majority role.

Thus, the correct characterization is given by option $\boxed{C}$.

71159.sol:
Common cold is a viral disease caused by Rhinovirus.

71445.subject: Biology
71445.text: If glucose is incompletely oxidized to ethyl alcohol in the absence of oxygen, the RQ will be ______.
71445.sol:
The chemical equation for the incomplete oxidation of glucose to ethyl alcohol in the absence of oxygen (anaerobic respiration) is given by:

$C_6H_{12}O_6 \rightarrow 2C_2H_5OH + 2CO_2 + \text{Energy}$

The respiratory quotient (RQ) is the ratio of the volume of carbon dioxide evolved to the volume of oxygen consumed during respiration.

$RQ = \dfrac{\text{Volume of } CO_2 \text{ evolved}}{\text{Volume of } O_2 \text{ consumed}}$

In this process, $2$ molecules of $CO_2$ are evolved while $0$ molecules of $O_2$ are consumed.

$RQ = \dfrac{2}{0} = \infty$

Thus, the RQ is infinite.

Answer: infinite
71445.meta: If glucose is incompletely oxidized to ethyl alcohol in the absence of oxygen, the RQ will be ______.

71463.subject: Biology
options: in cytoplasm of the cells only.
in cytoplasm of the cells and matrix of mitochondria.
71463.sol:
Substrate level phosphorylation is the direct synthesis of ATP from ADP by the transfer of a phosphate group from a phosphorylated reactive intermediate.

During glycolysis, which takes place in the cytoplasm, substrate level phosphorylation occurs at two steps: the conversion of $1,3$-bisphosphoglycerate to $3$-phosphoglyceric acid and the conversion of phosphoenolpyruvate to pyruvic acid.

During the Krebs cycle, which takes place in the mitochondrial matrix, substrate level phosphorylation occurs during the conversion of succinyl-CoA to succinic acid, where a molecule of GTP (which is then used to form ATP) is synthesized.

Therefore, substrate level phosphorylation occurs in both the cytoplasm of the cells and the matrix of mitochondria.

Answer: in cytoplasm of the cells and matrix of mitochondria.

72068.subject: Physics
72068.text:
The ratio of power factor of purely resistive circuit to purely reactive circuit is
(\cos 0^{}^{\circ} = 1$ and \cos 90^{}^{\circ} = 0$)
72068.sol:
The power factor of an AC circuit is given by $\cos \phi$, where $\phi$ is the phase difference between the voltage and the current.

For a purely resistive circuit, the voltage and current are in the same phase, so $\phi = 0^{}^{\circ}$.
Power factor $= \cos 0^{}^{\circ} = 1$

For a purely reactive circuit (purely inductive or purely capacitive), the phase difference between voltage and current is $\phi = 90^{}^{\circ}$.
Power factor $= \cos 90^{}^{\circ} = 0$

The ratio of the power factor of a purely resistive circuit to a purely reactive circuit is:
Ratio $= \dfrac{1}{0} = \infty$

Thus, the ratio is infinite.

Answer: infinite

72117.subject: Physics
72117.text: A capacitor of $2\ \mu\text{F}$ is charged as shown in the diagram. When the switch 'S' is turned to position 2, the percentage of its stored energy dissipated is
72117.sol:
Initial energy stored in the capacitor $C_1$ is:

$U_i = \dfrac{1}{2}C_1 V^2$

When the switch is turned to position 2, the charge is shared between $C_1$ and $C_2$. The common potential $V_c$ is:

$V_c = \dfrac{C_1 V}{C_1 + C_2}$

The final energy of the system is:

$U_f = \dfrac{1}{2}(C_1 + C_2)V_c^2 = \dfrac{1}{2}(C_1 + C_2)\left(\dfrac{C_1 V}{C_1 + C_2}\right)^2 = \dfrac{1}{2}\dfrac{C_1^2 V^2}{C_1 + C_2}$

The energy dissipated is:

$\Delta U = U_i - U_f = \dfrac{1}{2}C_1 V^2 - \dfrac{1}{2}\dfrac{C_1^2 V^2}{C_1 + C_2} = \dfrac{1}{2}\dfrac{C_1 C_2}{C_1 + C_2}V^2$

The percentage of stored energy dissipated is:

$\text{Percentage} = \dfrac{\Delta U}{U_i} \times 100 = \dfrac{\dfrac{1}{2}\dfrac{C_1 C_2}{C_1 + C_2}V^2}{\dfrac{1}{2}C_1 V^2} \times 100 = \dfrac{C_2}{C_1 + C_2} \times 100$

Given $C_1 = 2\ \mu\text{F}$ and $C_2 = 8\ \mu\text{F}$:

$\text{Percentage} = \dfrac{8}{2 + 8} \times 100 = \dfrac{8}{10} \times 100 = 80\%$

Answer: $80\ \%$

72264.subject: Physics
72264.text: The magnetic flux near the axis and inside the air core solenoid of length $60\ \text{cm}$ carrying current $'I'$ is $1.57 \times 10^{-6}\ \text{Wb}$. Its magnetic moment will be $\{cross-sectional area of a solenoid is very small as compared to its length, \mu_0 = 4\pi \times 10^{-7}\ \text{SI unit}\}$
72264.sol:
The magnetic field inside a long solenoid is given by:

$B = \dfrac{\mu_0 N I}{L}$

where $N$ is the total number of turns, $I$ is the current, and $L$ is the length of the solenoid.

The magnetic flux through the cross-section of the solenoid is:

$\Phi = B A = \dfrac{\mu_0 N I A}{L}$

The magnetic moment of a solenoid is given by:

$M = N I A$

Substituting $M$ into the flux equation, we get:

$\Phi = \dfrac{\mu_0 M}{L}$

Rearranging to solve for the magnetic moment $M$:

$M = \dfrac{\Phi L}{\mu_0}$

Given values are:
$\Phi = 1.57 \times 10^{-6}\ \text{Wb}$
$L = 60\ \text{cm} = 0.6\ \text{m}$
$\mu_0 = 4\pi \times 10^{-7}\ \text{T m/A} = 4 \times 3.14 \times 10^{-7}\ \text{T m/A} = 12.56 \times 10^{-7}\ \text{T m/A}$

Substituting these values into the formula:

$M = \dfrac{1.57 \times 10^{-6} \times 0.6}{12.56 \times 10^{-7}}$

$M = \dfrac{1.57}{12.56} \times 0.6 \times 10$

$M = \dfrac{1}{8} \times 6 = \dfrac{3}{4} = 0.75\ \text{A m}^2$

Answer: $0.75\ \text{Am}^2$

73898.subject: General Ability
73898.text:
In the following redox reaction, which compound is acting as a reducing agent?
$N_2H_4 + 2H_2O_2 \rightarrow N_2 + 4H_2O$
73898.sol:
In the given reaction, the oxidation state of nitrogen in $N_2H_4$ is $-2$ and it changes to $0$ in $N_2$. Since the oxidation state of nitrogen increases, $N_2H_4$ undergoes oxidation.

The oxidation state of oxygen in $H_2O_2$ is $-1$ and it changes to $-2$ in $H_2O$. Since the oxidation state of oxygen decreases, $H_2O_2$ undergoes reduction.

The species that undergoes oxidation acts as a reducing agent. Therefore, $N_2H_4$ is the reducing agent.

Answer: $N_2H_4$

75163.sol:
Volcanic ash consists of fine particles of fragmented volcanic rock and glass. When this ash is carried by running water and deposited as a sedimentary layer, it undergoes compaction and cementation over time.

The lithified rock formed from the consolidation of volcanic ash is known as tuff. Basalt is an extrusive igneous rock, lapilli refers to small volcanic fragments, and slate is a metamorphic rock.

Answer: Tuff

76380.subject: Mathematics
76380.text: For what value of $\theta$, where $0 < \theta < \frac{\pi}{2}$, does $\sin \theta+\sin \theta\cos \theta$ attain maximum value?
76380.sol:
$\begin{aligned} & \text{ Let } S=\sin \theta+\sin \theta \cdot \cos \theta \\ & \frac{d s}{d \theta}=\cos \theta+\cos ^2 \theta-\sin ^2 \theta \\ & =2 \cos ^2 \theta+\cos \theta-1=0 \\ & =(\cos \theta+1)(2 \cos \theta-1)=0 \\ & \therefore \cos \theta \neq 1 \therefore \cos \theta=\frac{1}{2} \Rightarrow \theta=\frac{\pi}{3}\end{aligned}$
Now, $\frac{d^2 s}{d \theta^2}=-4 \cos \theta \sin \theta-\sin \theta\left(\frac{d^2 s}{d \theta^2}\right)_{\left(x=\frac{\pi}{3}\right)}=-4 \times \frac{1}{2} \times \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}-\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2} < 0\therefore$ function is maximum at $x=\frac{\pi}{3}$

77087.subject: Mathematics
77087.text: What is the curve which passes through the point $(1,1)$ and whose slope is $\frac{2 \mathrm{y}}{\mathrm{x}} ?$
77087.sol:
$\begin{aligned}
& \frac{d y}{d x}=\frac{2 y}{x} \\
& \Rightarrow \frac{d y}{y}=2 \frac{d x}{x}
\end{aligned}$
On integration
$\begin{aligned}
& \int \frac{d y}{y}=2 \int \frac{d x}{x} \\
& \Rightarrow \log y=2 \log x+\log a \\
& \Rightarrow \log y=\log x^2+\log a \\
& \Rightarrow \log y=\log \left(x^2 \cdot a\right) \\
& \Rightarrow y=x^2 a \\
& \text{ at }(1,1) ; a=1 \\
& \Rightarrow x^2=y=4\left(\frac{1}{4}\right) y
\end{aligned}\Rightarrow$ the curve is parabola.

77447.text: From an aeroplane above a straight road the angles of depression of two positions at a distance 20 m apart on the road are observed to be $30^{{}^{\circ}}$ and $45^{{}^{\circ}}$. The height of the aeroplane above the ground is:
77447.sol: $\begin{array}{ll}\text{ In } \triangle \mathrm{ABD}, & \tan 45^{{}^{\circ}}=\frac{h}{x} \\ \Rightarrow & 1=\frac{h}{x} \Rightarrow h=x\end{array} In $\triangle $\mathrm{ABC}, \begin{array}{rlrl}$& & \tan 30^{{}^{\circ}} & =$\frac{h}{x+20}$\\ & \Rightarrow \quad $\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}$& =$\frac{h}{x+20}=\frac{h}{h+20} \quad(\because$x=h) \\ \Rightarrow & \quad $\sqrt{3}$h & =h+20=($\sqrt{3}$h-h)=20 \\ \Rightarrow & h($\sqrt{3}-$1) & =20 \\ \Rightarrow \quad & h & =$\frac{20}{\sqrt{3}-1} \times \frac{\sqrt{3}+1}{\sqrt{3}+1}=\frac{20(\sqrt{3}+1)}{2}$\\ \Rightarrow \quad & h & =10($\sqrt{3}+$1) \end{array} Hence, height of the aeroplane above the ground $=10(\sqrt{3}+1) \mathrm{m}$.

80442.subject: Botany
80442.text: Chemiosmotic theory of ATP synthesis in the chloroplasts and mitochondria is based on:
80442.sol:
According to the chemiosmosis theory of ATP generation. The ATP is generated utilizing the electrochemical gradient generated due to the accumulation of protons in the thylakoid lumen of chloroplast or peri-mitochondrial space in mitochondria. The accumulation of protons gives rise to an electric gradient, due to the accumulation of positive charge and a chemical gradient due to the accumulation of hydrogen atom.
Related Theory
The chemiosmotic hypothesis stated that a proton-motive force was responsible for driving the synthesis of ATP. In this hypothesis, protons would be pumped across the inner mitochondrial membrane as electrons went through the electron transfer chain. This would result in a proton gradient with a lower $\mathrm{pH}$ in the intermembrane space and an elevated $\mathrm{pH}$ in the matrix of the mitochondria. An intact inner mitochondrial membrane, impermeable to protons, is a requirement of such a model. The proton gradient and membrane potential are the proton-motive force that is used to drive ATP synthesis. In effect, the pH gradient acts as $a$ "battery" which stores energy to produce ATP.

85346.subject: Zoology
85346.text: Lack of independent assortment of two genes A and B in fruit fly Drosophila is due to:
85346.sol:
Sex linkage was discovered by Thomas H. Morgan. He discovered it by conducting experiments on eye character in fruit fly, Drosophila. Independent assortment of genes does not occur during cell division.
Related Theory
Coupling and repulsion are two aspects of gene linkages. Coupling is the presence of two dominant alleles of two genes on the same chromosome $(A B)$. The remaining recessive genes of the two genes are present on the other chromosome (ab). Hence, the dominant alleles of genes tend to remain together. Repulsion is the presence of dominant genes on the two homologous chromosomes (Ab/aB).

90110.sol:
Let $\dfrac{y}{x} = {m}^{'}$. So, on putting $y = {m}^{′} x$ in the given circle,
We get ${\left(x - 3\right)}^{2} + {\left({m}^{′} x - 3\right)}^{2} = 6$
$⇒ {x}^{2}\left(1 + {m}^{{'}^{}2}\right) - 6x\left(1 + {m}^{'}\right) + 12 = 0$
Putting discriminant $= 0$, we get,
${m}^{'} = 3\mathop{+}_{_}2\sqrt{2}$
So, m = $3 - 2\sqrt{2}$ and $M = 3 + 2\sqrt{2} ⇒ mM = 1$
$⇒ \dfrac{1}{M} + \dfrac{1}{m} = m + M$
$= 3 - 2\sqrt{2} + 3 + 2\sqrt{2}$
$= 6$

Since, ${sec}^{2} ⁡ \alpha + {cosec}^{2} ⁡ \alpha - 3 = \left(1 + \tan^{2} ⁡ \alpha\right) + \left(1 + {cot}^{2} ⁡ \alpha\right) - 3$

Now, the minimum distance

$= \sqrt{4 + {\left(tan ⁡ \alpha - cot ⁡ \alpha\right)}^{2}} - \sqrt{3}$ (Minimum is attained, when $tan ⁡ \alpha = cot ⁡ \alpha$)
$= 2 - \sqrt{3} ≡ a - \sqrt{b}$ (Given)
So, $a = 2, b = 3 .$

Hence, $\dfrac{b}{a} = \dfrac{3}{2} = 1.5$

91823.text: Three numbers $a, b$~and& $c$ are in geometric progression. If~$4a, 5b$~and& $4c$ are in arithmetic progression and $a + b + c = 70$, then the value of~$\left|c - a\right|$ is equal to
91823.sol:
$a + b + c = 70$
$⇒ a + ar + ar^{2} = 70$
Also, $10b = 4a + 4c$
$⇒ 10ar = 4a + 4ar^{2}$
$⇒ 2r^{2} - 5r + 2 = 0 ⇒ r = 2, \dfrac{1}{2}$
For $r = 2$, we have,
$a\left(1 + r + r^{2}\right) = 70 ⇒ a = \dfrac{70}{1 + r + r^{2}} = \dfrac{70}{1 + 2 + 4} = 10$
$⇒ a = 10, b = 20, c = 40 ⇒ \left|c - a\right| = 30$
For $r = \dfrac{1}{2}$, we have,
$a = \dfrac{70}{1 + r + r^{2}} = \dfrac{70}{1 + \dfrac{1}{2} + \dfrac{1}{4}} = \dfrac{70 \times 4}{4 + 2 + 1} = 40$
$⇒ b = 20, c = 10$
$⇒ \left|c - a\right| = \left|10 - 40\right| = 30$
So, in both the cases $\left|c - a\right| = 30$

96635.text:
The definition given below describes:

"The mass of living material at a trophic level at a particular time."
96635.sol:
Standing crop is the total amount of living material in a specified population at a particular time, generally expressed as biomass. The standing crop may show variation at different times of the year.

Net Primary Productivity (NPP) is the rate at which plants incorporate atmospheric carbon through photosynthesis. (Definition)

Gross primary production (GPP) is the rate at which an ecosystem's producers capture and store a given amount of chemical energy as biomass in a given length of time. (Definition)

100516.subject: Physics
100516.text: A grindstone of moment of inertia $5 \text{ kg m}^2$ is rotating at $600 \text{ rpm}$. A constant retarding torque of $10\pi \text{ N m}$ is applied to it. The number of complete revolutions the grindstone makes before coming to rest is
100516.sol:
Given, initial angular velocity $\omega_i = 600 \text{ rpm} = 600 \times \dfrac{2\pi}{60} \text{ rad/s} = 20\pi \text{ rad/s}$
Final angular velocity $\omega_f = 0$
Moment of inertia $I = 5 \text{ kg m}^2$
Retarding torque $\tau = 10\pi \text{ N m}$

The angular deceleration $\alpha$ is:
$\alpha = \dfrac{\tau}{I} = \dfrac{10\pi}{5} = 2\pi \text{ rad/s}^2$

Using the third equation of rotational kinematics:
$\omega_f^2 = \omega_i^2 - 2\alpha\theta$
$0 = (20\pi)^2 - 2(2\pi)\theta$
$4\pi\theta = 400\pi^2$
$\theta = 100\pi \text{ rad}$

The number of complete revolutions $n$ is:
$n = \dfrac{\theta}{2\pi} = \dfrac{100\pi}{2\pi} = 50$

Answer: $50$

100938.subject: Physics
100938.text: A particle is thrown vertically upwards with velocity $11.2 \mathrm{~km} \mathrm{~s}^{-1}$ from the surface of earth. Calculate its velocity at height $3 R$. Where $R$ is the radius of earth.
100938.sol:
Let a particle of mass $m$ is thrown vertically upward with velocity $v$. Let its velocity be $v^{\prime}$ at a height $3 R$ from the surface of the earth. According to the conservation of energy,
$\frac{1}{2} m v^2-\frac{G M m}{R}=\frac{1}{2} m v^{\prime 2}-\frac{G M m}{(R+3 R)}$
$v^2-\frac{2 G M}{R}=v^{\prime 2}-\frac{2 G M}{4 R}$
$v^2-v^{\prime 2}=\frac{-2 G M}{4 R}+\frac{2 G M}{R}=\frac{6}{4} \frac{G M}{R}$
$v^{\prime 2}=v^2-\frac{6}{4} \frac{G M}{R}$
$v^{\prime 2}=\sqrt{(11.2)^2-\frac{3}{2} g R} \quad\left(\because g=\frac{G M}{R^2}\right)$
$=\sqrt{(11.2)^2-\frac{3}{2} \times \frac{9.8 \times 6400}{1000}}$
$=\sqrt{(11.2)^2-(94.08)}$
$=5.6 \mathrm{~km} \mathrm{~s}^{-1}$

101380.subject: Physics
101380.text: Two planets have escape velocities in the ratio $2 : 1$ and acceleration due to gravity at their surfaces in the ratio $1 : 2$. The ratio of their radii is:
101380.sol:
The escape velocity $v_e$ is related to the acceleration due to gravity $g$ and radius $R$ by the formula $v_e = \sqrt{2gR}$.

Rearranging this for the radius gives $R = \dfrac{v_e^2}{2g}$.

Therefore, the ratio of the radii of the two planets is:
$\dfrac{R_1}{R_2} = \left(\dfrac{v_1}{v_2}\right)^2 \times \left(\dfrac{g_2}{g_1}\right)$

Given $\dfrac{v_1}{v_2} = \dfrac{2}{1}$ and $\dfrac{g_1}{g_2} = \dfrac{1}{2}$ (which implies $\dfrac{g_2}{g_1} = \dfrac{2}{1}$):

$\dfrac{R_1}{R_2} = (2)^2 \times (2) = 4 \times 2 = 8$

The ratio of their radii is $8 : 1$.

Answer: $8 : 1$

101557.subject: Physics
101557.text: A cylindrical wire of length $L$ and diameter $D$ is subjected to a longitudinal stretching force $F$. If the material of the wire has a Young's modulus $Y$ and a Poisson's ratio $\sigma$, which of the following represents the magnitude of the decrease in its diameter ($\Delta D$)?
101557.sol:
Longitudinal stress is given by $\dfrac{F}{A}$, where $A = \dfrac{\pi D^2}{4}$.

From the definition of Young's modulus ($Y$), the longitudinal strain is:
$\dfrac{\Delta L}{L} = \dfrac{F}{A Y} = \dfrac{4F}{\pi D^2 Y}$

Poisson's ratio ($\sigma$) is the ratio of lateral strain to longitudinal strain:
$\sigma = \dfrac{\Delta D / D}{\Delta L / L}$

Rearranging for the lateral strain:
$\dfrac{\Delta D}{D} = \sigma \left(\dfrac{\Delta L}{L}\right) = \sigma \left(\dfrac{4F}{\pi D^2 Y}\right)$

Therefore, the magnitude of the decrease in diameter is:
$\Delta D = D \times \dfrac{4F\sigma}{\pi D^2 Y} = \dfrac{4F\sigma}{\pi D Y}$

Answer: $\dfrac{4F\sigma}{\pi D Y}$

103317.subject: Physics
103317.text: A uniform heating wire of resistance $R$ produces thermal energy $H$ in time $t$ when connected directly across a constant voltage battery. The wire is now cut into three equal pieces, and these pieces are connected in parallel across the same battery. The thermal energy produced by this parallel combination in the same time $t$ will be
103317.sol:
The initial thermal energy produced by the wire is given by $H = \dfrac{V^2}{R}t$.

When the uniform wire is cut into three equal pieces, the resistance of each piece becomes $\dfrac{R}{3}$ because resistance is directly proportional to length.

When these three pieces are connected in parallel, their equivalent resistance $R_{eq}$ is calculated as:
$\dfrac{1}{R_{eq}} = \dfrac{1}{R/3} + \dfrac{1}{R/3} + \dfrac{1}{R/3} = \dfrac{3}{R} + \dfrac{3}{R} + \dfrac{3}{R} = \dfrac{9}{R}$

Thus, $R_{eq} = \dfrac{R}{9}$.

The new thermal energy produced in the same time $t$ across the same battery is:
$H' = \dfrac{V^2}{R_{eq}}t = \dfrac{V^2}{R/9}t = 9 \left(\dfrac{V^2}{R}t\right) = 9H$.

A common mistake is calculating the resistance of one piece as $R/3$ and using it directly to get $3H$, forgetting to combine all three pieces in parallel.

Answer: $9H$

105555.subject: Physics
105555.text: In a photoelectric experiment, the macroscopic intensity of the incident light (measured in $\text{W/m}^2$) is kept strictly constant. If the wavelength of the incident light is continuously decreased (while remaining below the threshold wavelength), how will the magnitude of the stopping potential and the saturation photocurrent change?
options: Both the magnitude of stopping potential and the saturation photocurrent increase.
The magnitude of stopping potential increases, while the saturation photocurrent remains constant.
The magnitude of stopping potential increases, while the saturation photocurrent decreases.
The magnitude of stopping potential decreases, while the saturation photocurrent increases.
105555.sol:
The magnitude of the stopping potential $|V|$ is given by $e|V| = \dfrac{hc}{\lambda} - \Phi$. As the wavelength $\lambda$ decreases, the energy of each incident photon increases, which causes the stopping potential to increase.

The macroscopic intensity of light is the total energy incident per unit area per unit time, given by $I = \dfrac{n h c}{\lambda A}$, where $n$ is the number of photons incident per second.

Since the macroscopic intensity $I$ is kept constant and $\lambda$ is decreased, the energy per photon ($\dfrac{hc}{\lambda}$) increases. To maintain a constant total energy per second, the number of incident photons per second ($n$) must decrease.

The saturation photocurrent is directly proportional to the number of incident photons per second. Therefore, the saturation photocurrent decreases.

Answer: The magnitude of stopping potential increases, while the saturation photocurrent decreases.

107556.subject: Chemistry
107556.text:
Identify the correct statements from the following :
a) Change in hybridisation affects the electronegativity of carbon
b) The p orbitals in ethene are mutually parallel
c) The number of $\sigma$ bonds in propyne is 6
d) Electromeric effect is a permanent effect
107556.sol:
Statements a, b, and c are correct.
- a) Change in hybridization affects electronegativity. Carbon's electronegativity increases with the percentage of s-character in its hybridization \($\left($s p \gt s p² \gt s p³\right)\).
- b) The p orbitals in ethene are parallel. The two unhybridized p-orbitals on the \(s p²\) hybridized carbon atoms are parallel to each other, allowing for side-by-side overlap to form the pi bond.
- c) Propyne has 6 sigma bonds. The structure (\(C H_3-C $\equiv$C H\)) contains three \($\mathrm{C}-\mathrm{H}$\) bonds, one \($\mathrm{C}-\mathrm{C}$\) single bond, and one \($\mathrm{C}-\mathrm{C}$\) bond within the triple bond, and one \($\mathrm{C}-\mathrm{H}$\) bond, for a total of 6 sigma bonds.
- d) The electromeric effect is a temporary effect. It only occurs in the presence of an attacking reagent.
Thus, the correct statements are a, b, and c.

107714.subject: Chemistry
107714.text: Which of the following statements regarding the nitrogen molecule and its ions is correct?
options: During the conversion of $\text{N}_2$ to $\text{N}_2^+$, the bond order decreases and the species becomes paramagnetic.
In the formation of $\text{N}_2^-$ from $\text{N}_2$, the additional electron enters a bonding molecular orbital.
The bond order of $\text{N}_2^+$ is greater than that of $\text{N}_2$ because an electron is removed from an antibonding molecular orbital.
Both $\text{N}_2^+$ and $\text{N}_2^-$ are diamagnetic species because their bond orders are identical.
107714.sol:
According to Molecular Orbital Theory:

$\text{N}_2$ ($14$ electrons) has the configuration: $\sigma 1s^2 \sigma^{*} 1s^2 \sigma 2s^2 \sigma^{*} 2s^2 \pi 2p_x^2 = \pi 2p_y^2 \sigma 2p_z^2$.
Its bond order is $\dfrac{10 - 4}{2} = 3$. Since all electrons are paired, it is diamagnetic.

When $\text{N}_2$ is converted to $\text{N}_2^+$ ($13$ electrons), an electron is removed from the bonding molecular orbital ($\sigma 2p_z$).
The new bond order becomes $\dfrac{9 - 4}{2} = 2.5$. The presence of one unpaired electron makes $\text{N}_2^+$ paramagnetic. Thus, the bond order decreases and the magnetic nature changes from diamagnetic to paramagnetic.

When $\text{N}_2$ is converted to $\text{N}_2^-$ ($15$ electrons), the extra electron enters an antibonding molecular orbital ($\pi^{*} 2p_x$ or $\pi^{*} 2p_y$). This makes $\text{N}_2^-$ paramagnetic with a bond order of $2.5$.

Therefore, only the first statement is correct.

Answer: During the conversion of $\text{N}_2$ to $\text{N}_2^+$, the bond order decreases and the species becomes paramagnetic.

107749.subject: Chemistry
107749.text:
Given below are four statements regarding the bonding in various molecules:
(A) A molecule of water contains $2\ \sigma$ bonds and $2$ lone pairs on the central atom.
(B) A molecule of carbon dioxide contains $2\ \sigma$ bonds and $2\ \pi$ bonds.
(C) A molecule of hydrogen cyanide contains $2\ \sigma$ bonds and $1\ \pi$ bond.
(D) A molecule of benzene contains $12\ \sigma$ bonds and $3\ \pi$ bonds.

How many of the above statements are correct?
107749.sol:
Let us evaluate each statement:

(A) Water ($\text{H}_2\text{O}$) has a central oxygen atom bonded to two hydrogen atoms via single bonds ($2\ \sigma$ bonds). Oxygen has $6$ valence electrons; $2$ are shared and $4$ remain as non-bonding electrons, forming $2$ lone pairs. This statement is correct.

(B) Carbon dioxide ($\text{CO}_2$) has the structure $\text{O}=\text{C}=\text{O}$. Each double bond consists of $1\ \sigma$ and $1\ \pi$ bond. Thus, there are $2\ \sigma$ and $2\ \pi$ bonds in total. This statement is correct.

(C) Hydrogen cyanide ($\text{HCN}$) has the structure $\text{H}-\text{C}\equiv\text{N}$. It contains one single bond ($1\ \sigma$) and one triple bond ($1\ \sigma$ and $2\ \pi$). The total is $2\ \sigma$ and $2\ \pi$ bonds. The statement claims it has $1\ \pi$ bond, so it is incorrect.

(D) Benzene ($\text{C}_6\text{H}_6$) consists of a hexagonal ring with alternating single and double bonds. It contains $6\ \text{C}-\text{C}$ single/double bond frameworks ($6\ \sigma$ bonds), $6\ \text{C}-\text{H}$ single bonds ($6\ \sigma$ bonds), and $3$ double bonds ($3\ \pi$ bonds). Total bonds: $12\ \sigma$ and $3\ \pi$ bonds. This statement is correct.

There are $3$ correct statements (A, B, and D).

Answer: $3$

$\begin{aligned}
\mathrm{M}_1 & =0.2 \mathrm{M}, \mathrm{N}_1=0.2 \mathrm{ N} \\
\mathrm{M}_2 & =0.1 \mathrm{M}, \mathrm{N}_2=0.1 \mathrm{ N} \\
\mathrm{ V}_1 & =50 \mathrm{ml}, \\
\mathrm{V}_2 & =50 \mathrm{ml}, \mathrm{V}_{\text{mix }}=100 \mathrm{ml}
\end{aligned}$
On substituting the given values is equation. (i), We get
$\begin{aligned}
\mathrm{N}_{\text{mix }} \times 100 & =50 \times 0.2-50 \times 0.1 \\
\mathrm{ N}_{\text{mix }} & =\frac{5}{100}=5 \times 10^{-2} \\
\therefore \quad\left[\mathrm{OH}^{-}\right] & =5 \times 10^{-2}
\end{aligned}$
Now,
$\begin{aligned}
{ }_{\mathrm{P}} \mathrm{OH} & =-\log \left[\mathrm{OH}^{-}\right]=-\log \left[5 \times 10^{-2}\right] \\
& =2-\log 5=1.3
\end{aligned}$
Also, $\mathrm{pH}+\mathrm{pOH}=14 \mathrm{pH}=14-1.3=12.7$

109818.text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): The oxidation state of sulphur in $\mathrm{H_2S_2O_8}$ (Marshall's acid) is +6.
Reason (R): $\mathrm{H_2S_2O_8}$ contains one peroxide linkage ($-\mathrm{O}-\mathrm{O}-$) in its structure.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are correct but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation for Assertion (A)
Assertion (A) is correct but Reason (R) is incorrect
Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are correct and Reason (R) is the correct explanation for Assertion (A)
Assertion (A) is incorrect but Reason (R) is correct
109818.sol:
Assertion (A) is correct: The maximum oxidation state of sulphur (Group 16) cannot exceed +6. In $\mathrm{H_2S_2O_8}$, the oxidation state of sulphur is indeed +6.

Reason (R) is correct and explains Assertion (A): If the oxidation state of sulphur is calculated algebraically assuming all oxygen atoms are in the -2 oxidation state, the result is $2x + 8(-2) = 0 \Rightarrow x = +8$, which is impossible. The structure of Marshall's acid is $\mathrm{HO-SO_2-O-O-SO_2-OH}$. It contains one peroxide linkage ($-\mathrm{O}-\mathrm{O}-$) where two oxygen atoms have an oxidation state of -1.

Calculating correctly: $2x + 6(-2) + 2(-1) = 0 \Rightarrow 2x - 14 = 0 \Rightarrow x = +6$. Thus, the presence of the peroxide linkage explains why the oxidation state is +6 rather than the algebraically calculated +8.

Answer: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are correct and Reason (R) is the correct explanation for Assertion (A)

114354.text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): The limiting molar conductivity ($\Lambda_m^\circ$) of a weak electrolyte like acetic acid cannot be determined accurately by extrapolating the plot of $\Lambda_m$ against $\sqrt{c}$ to zero concentration.
Reason (R): The degree of dissociation of a weak electrolyte decreases significantly upon dilution.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
114354.sol:
Assertion (A) is true. For weak electrolytes, the plot of $\Lambda_m$ against $\sqrt{c}$ shows a steep increase in molar conductivity at low concentrations. Therefore, it does not yield a straight line that can be extrapolated to zero concentration to find $\Lambda_m^\circ$.

Reason (R) is false. According to Ostwald's dilution law, the degree of dissociation of a weak electrolyte increases significantly upon dilution, which is the actual reason for the steep increase in molar conductivity at lower concentrations.

Therefore, (A) is true but (R) is false.

Answer: (A) is true but (R) is false

119270.subject: Chemistry
119270.text:
Consider the following two-step reaction sequence:
Benzoyl chloride $\xrightarrow{\text{H}_2/\text{Pd-BaSO}_4}$ A
A $\xrightarrow{\text{conc. NaOH, }\Delta}$ B + C

Identify the final products B and C.
119270.sol:
Step 1: Benzoyl chloride undergoes Rosenmund reduction in the presence of $\text{H}_2$ and $\text{Pd-BaSO}_4$ to form benzaldehyde (Intermediate A).

Step 2: Benzaldehyde lacks $\alpha$-hydrogen atoms. When heated with concentrated NaOH, it undergoes the Cannizzaro reaction (disproportionation). One molecule is reduced to benzyl alcohol, and another is oxidized to sodium benzoate.

Therefore, products B and C are benzyl alcohol and sodium benzoate. Benzoic acid is not formed directly because the reaction occurs in a strongly basic medium, which yields the carboxylate salt.

Answer: Benzyl alcohol and sodium benzoate

122204.subject: Botany
122204.text: What is the function of the mouth on the hypostome in cnidarians?
122204.sol: Cnidarians exhibit tissue level of organization and are diploblastic. Cnidoblasts, also known as cnidocytes, contain stinging capsules or nematocysts and are used for anchorage, defense, and prey capture in cnidarians. Cnidarians exhibit two basic body forms called polyp and medusa Cnidarians have a central gastrovascular cavity with a single opening, mouth on hypostome, for food intake. Digestion is extracellular and intracellular. Some of the cnidarians, e.g., corals have a skeleton composed of calcium carbonate. Cnidarians exhibit two basic body forms called polyp and medusa (Figure 4.6). The former is a sessile and cylindrical form like Hydra, Adamsia, etc. whereas, the latter is umbrella-shaped and free-swimming like Aurelia or jelly fish. Those cnidarians which exist in both forms exhibit alternation of generation (Metagenesis), i.e., polyps produce medusae asexually and medusae form the polyps sexually (e.g., Obelia).

123233.subject: Botany
123233.text: What is the structure of the innermost layer of the cortex?
123233.sol: The transverse section of a typical young dicotyledonous stem shows that the epidermis is the outermost protective layer of the stem Covered with a thin layer of cuticle, it may bear trichomes and a few stomata. The cells arranged in multiple layers between epidermis and pericycle constitute the cortex. It consists of three sub-zones. The outer hypodermis, consists of a few layers of collenchymatous cells just below the epidermis, which provide mechanical strength to the young stem. Cortical layers below hypodermis consist of rounded thin walled parenchymatous cells with conspicuous intercellular spaces. The innermost layer of the cortex is called the endodermis. The cells of the endodermis are rich in starch grains and the layer is also referred to as the starch sheath. Pericycle is present on the inner side of the endodermis and above the phloem in the form of semi-lunar patches of sclerenchyma. In between the vascular bundles there are a few layers of radially placed parenchymatous cells, which constitute medullary rays. A large number of vascular bundles are arranged in a ring ; the ‘ring’ arrangement of vascular bundles is a characteristic of dicot stem. Each vascular bundle is conjoint, open, and with endarch protoxylem. A large number of rounded, parenchymatous cells with large intercellularspaces which occupy the central portion of the stem constitute the pith.

123642.subject: Botany
123642.text: Which of the following is not a key feature of mitosis?
options: The division of the cell into two daughter cells
123642.sol: In an animal cell, this is achieved by the appearance of a furrow in the plasma membrane. The furrow gradually deepens and ultimately joins in the centre dividing the cell cytoplasm into two. Plant cells however, are enclosed by a relatively inextensible cell wall, thererfore they undergo cytokinesis by a different mechanism. In plant cells, wall formation starts in the centre of the cell and grows outward to meet the existing lateral walls. The formation of the new cell wall begins with the formation of a simple precursor, called the cell-plate that represents the middle lamella between the walls of two adjacent cells. At the time of cytoplasmic division, organelles like mitochondria and plastids get distributed between the two daughter cells. In some organisms karyokinesis is not followed by cytokinesis as a result of which multinucleate condition arises leading to the formation of syncytium (e.g., liquid endosperm in coconut).

124321.subject: Botany
124321.text:
Match List I with List II regarding the historical contributions to cell biology.

List I (Scientists)List II (Discoveries/Statements)
A. M. SchleidenI. First saw and described a live cell
B. T. SchwannII. Omnis cellula-e cellula
C. R. VirchowIII. Reported that cells have a thin outer layer
D. Anton Von LeeuwenhoekIV. Observed that all plants are composed of different kinds of cells

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
124321.sol:
According to NCERT:

M. Schleiden (1838), a German botanist, observed that all plants are composed of different kinds of cells (A-IV).

T. Schwann (1839), a British zoologist, studied animal cells and reported that cells had a thin outer layer, today known as the plasma membrane (B-III).

R. Virchow (1855) first explained that cells divide and new cells are formed from pre-existing cells, encapsulated in the phrase 'Omnis cellula-e cellula' (C-II).

Anton Von Leeuwenhoek first saw and described a live cell (D-I).

Therefore, the correct matching is A-IV, B-III, C-II, D-I. Swapping the contributions of Schleiden and Schwann is a common mistake, as is confusing Leeuwenhoek's observation with Schwann's.

Answer: A-IV, B-III, C-II, D-I

125007.text: What forms the channel through which protons cross the inner membrane in ATP synthase?
125007.sol: This complex consists of two major components, F1 and F0 (Figure 12.5). The F1 headpiece is a peripheral membrane protein complex and contains the site for synthesis of ATP from ADP and inorganic phosphate. F0 is an integral membrane protein complex that forms the channel through which protons cross the inner membrane. The passage of protons through the channel is coupled to the catalytic site of the F1 component for the production of ATP. For each ATP produced, 4H+ passes through F0 from the intermembrane space to the matrix down the electrochemical proton gradient.

125259.text: Nicotiana sylvestris flowers only during long days and N.tabacum flowers only during short days. If raised in the laboratory under different photoperiods, they can be induced to flower at the same time and can be cross-fertilized to produce self-fertile offspring. What is the best reason for considering \(N\).sylvestris and N.tabacum to be separate species?
125259.sol: The process by which $\mathrm{N}_2$ is reduced to $\mathrm{NH}_4^{+}$ is called nitrogen fixation. Nitrogenase enzyme catalyzes this reduction. It is only carried out by prokaryotic microorganisms. Principal $\mathrm{N}_2$-fixers include certain free living cyanobacteria in symbiotic associations with fungi in lichens or with ferns, mosses, and liverworts, and by bacteria or other microbes associated symbiotically with roots, especially those of legumes. About 15 percent of the nearly 20,000 species in the fabaceae (Leguminosae) family have been examined for $\mathrm{N}_2$ fixation, and approximately 90 percent of these have root nodules in which fixation occurs. So without active nitrogenase enzyme there will be no $\mathrm{N}_2$ fixation in legumes.

125812.text: What is the process of formation of microspores from a pollen mother cell through meiosis called?

(iii) Water lily
(iv) Zostera

In which of the above plants do the flowers emerge above the level of water and are pollinated by insects or wind?
126257.sol:
Not all aquatic plants use water for pollination. In a majority of aquatic plants such as Water hyacinth and Water lily, the flowers emerge above the level of water and are pollinated by insects or wind, similar to most land plants.

Vallisneria and Zostera are examples of water-pollinated plants. In Vallisneria, the female flower reaches the surface of water and pollination occurs at the surface. In Zostera (marine seagrass), the female flowers remain submerged and pollination occurs entirely inside the water.

Answer: (i) and (iii) only

128352.subject: Zoology
128352.text: What hormone is produced by the adrenal medulla?
128352.sol: The adrenal medulla secretes two hormones called adrenaline or epinephrine and noradrenaline or norepinephrine. These are commonly called as catecholamines. Adrenaline and noradrenaline are rapidly secreted in response to stress of any kind and during emergency situations and are called emergency hormones or hormones of Fight or Flight. These hormones increase alertness, pupilary dilation, piloerection (raising of hairs), sweating etc. Both the hormones increase the heart beat, the strength of heart contraction and the rate of respiration. Catecholamines also stimulate the breakdown of glycogen resulting in an increased concentration of glucose in blood. In addition, they also stimulate the breakdown of lipids and proteins.Pancreas is a composite gland (Figure 19.1) which acts as both exocrine and endocrine gland. The endocrine pancreas consists of ‘Islets of Langerhans’. There are about 1 to 2 million Islets of Langerhans in a normal human pancreas representing only 1 to 2 per cent of the pancreatictissue. The two main types of cells in the Islet of Langerhans are calledα-cells and β-cells. The α-cells secrete a hormone called glucagon, while the β-cells secrete insulin.Prolonged hyperglycemia leads to a complex disorder called diabetes mellitus which is associated with loss of glucose through urine and formation of harmful compounds known as ketone bodies. Diabetic patients are successfully treated with insulin therapy.

130242.subject: Zoology
130242.text: What is the name of the U-shaped bone present at the base of the buccal cavity?
130242.sol: The Skeletal system is grouped into two main divisions - the axial skeleton which includes the bones that make up the central axis of the body such as the skull, spinal column, rib cage and the appendicular skeleton which includes bones of the upper and lower limbs and the bones that attach the limbs to the axial skeleton. Bones play a crucial role in supporting and providing structure to the human body. They also protect delicate organs, store minerals, and produce blood cells. The human body consists of 206 bones in total. These bones are grouped into two main divisions - the axial skeleton and the appendicular skeleton. The skull is composed of two sets of bones, cranial and facial, that total to 22 bones. A single U-shaped bone called hyoid is present at the base of the buccal cavity and is also included in the skull.

130829.subject: Zoology
130829.text: What do the Leydig cells in the testis secrete?
130829.sol: Each lobule contains one to three highly coiled seminiferous tubules in which sperms are produced. Each seminiferous tubule is lined on its inside by two types of cells called male germ cells (spermatogonia) and Sertoli cells. The male germ cells undergo meiotic divisions finally leading to sperm formation, while Sertoli cells provide nutrition to the germ cells. The regions outside the seminiferous tubules called interstitial spaces, contain small blood vessels and interstitial cells or Leydig cells. Leydig cells synthesise and secrete testicular hormones called androgens. Other immunologically competent cells are also present

130877.subject: Zoology
130877.text: What are the primary sex organs in males?
130877.sol: The primary sex organs – the testis in the males and the ovaries in the females–produce gametes, i.e, sperms and ovum, respectively, by the process called gametogenesis. In testis, the immature male germ cells (spermatogonia) produce sperms by spermatogenesis that begins at puberty. The spermatogonia (sing. spermatogonium) present on the inside wall of seminiferous tubules multiply by mitotic division and increase in numbers. Each spermatogonium is diploid and contains 46 chromosomes. Some of the spermatogonia called primary spermatocytes periodically undergo meiosis. A primary spermatocyte completes the first meiotic division (reduction division) leading to formation of two equal, haploid cells called secondary spermatocytes, which have only 23 chromosomes each.

131196.subject: Zoology
131196.text:
Read the following paragraph and identify the hormones and processes labelled as [A], [B], [C], and [D].

At puberty, increased levels of GnRH stimulate the anterior pituitary to secrete two gonadotropins. Hormone [A] acts on Leydig cells to stimulate the synthesis of androgens, which in turn stimulate the process of [B]. Hormone [C] acts on Sertoli cells to stimulate secretion of some factors which help in the process of [D].

Choose the correct option :
131196.sol:
According to NCERT, at puberty, GnRH stimulates the anterior pituitary to release two gonadotropins: LH and FSH.

LH (Luteinising Hormone) acts on the Leydig cells to stimulate the synthesis and secretion of androgens. Androgens then stimulate the entire process of spermatogenesis.

FSH (Follicle Stimulating Hormone) acts on the Sertoli cells and stimulates the secretion of some factors which help in the process of spermiogenesis (the transformation of spermatids into spermatozoa).

Therefore, [A] is LH, [B] is spermatogenesis, [C] is FSH, and [D] is spermiogenesis.

Answer: [A] - LH, [B] - spermatogenesis, [C] - FSH, [D] - spermiogenesis
